lesson.title: Meeting the Letter A (Our First Vowel!)
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You know two letter sounds now: S and M. Today is special — we're meeting our very first vowel, the letter A! Vowels are extra important because almost every word needs at least one.

The short A sound is like the 'a' in 'cat' or 'apple': aaa. Say 'aaa' together and notice how your mouth opens wide. Now try some words with that sound: apple, ant, cat, hat. Say each word slowly, listening for the 'aaa' sound in the middle or start: aaa-pple, aaa-nt, c-aaa-t, h-aaa-t.
You just met your first vowel! Vowels are the glue that holds words together. Tomorrow we'll meet one more letter — and then we'll blend sounds into a real word.

objectives: Identify the letter A and produce its short vowel sound (/a/ as in 'cat')
Recognize the /a/ sound in familiar words, whether at the start or in the middle
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Explain simply that A is a vowel, and vowels are extra important because almost every word has one.
2. Model the short A sound: 'aaa', with your mouth open wide.
3. Say a list of words slowly, listening for /a/: apple, ant, cat, hat. Ask the child to give a thumbs up when they hear it.
4. Point out that in 'cat' and 'hat', the A sound is in the middle, not just the start — this is a bit trickier than S and M.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace the letter A, then practice writing it once more.
6. Close by brainstorming one more word with the /a/ sound.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus only on words where A starts the word (apple, ant) before tackling middle-of-word examples like cat and hat
Ready for more: introduce that this is called the 'short A' sound, and that A can make other sounds too, which they'll learn later
For a child who already writes letters confidently, have them write a full row of A's from memory before tracing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and sound-recognition activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct letter formation and hearing the /a/ sound.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Introducing the first vowel alongside two consonants (S, M) is a standard early-literacy sequencing choice — it sets up real word-blending (S + A + T = 'sat') by the end of this week.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.

rows.label: Lowercase a — same sound, smaller letter
